speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for stating your symptoms of right knee swelling and your family history. To begin our evaluation, can you describe exactly when the swelling started and what specific activities seem to trigger or worsen it?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pseudotumor of the Knee (Synovial Hemangioma). Given the patient's age (18 months), the lack of trauma, the isolated unilateral swelling, and the strong family history, this is highly suggestive of a vascular malformation of the synovium rather than a traumatic effusion or infection. I am requesting a MRI of the right knee to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other pathologies.
